header:
What a strong dollar
means for you

lines.text: A strong dollar sounds like good news. It's more complicated than that.
lines.say: A strong dollar sounds like good news. It's more complicated than that.

lines.text: It means one dollar buys more of other currencies.
lines.say: It means one dollar buys more of other currencies.

lines.text: Take a 100 euro hotel room. At a dollar ten per euro, it costs you 110 dollars.
lines.say: Take a one hundred euro hotel room. At a dollar ten per euro, it costs you one hundred and ten dollars.

lines.text: At a dollar twenty-five, the same room costs 125. The stronger dollar saves you 15.
lines.say: At a dollar twenty-five, the same room costs one hundred and twenty-five. The stronger dollar saves you fifteen.

lines.text: It's good for travelers and imported goods. It's harder for U.S. companies selling abroad.
lines.say: It's good for travelers and imported goods. It's harder for U.S. companies selling abroad.

lines.text: And exchange rates move every trading day, so this changes all the time.
lines.say: And exchange rates move every trading day, so this changes all the time.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.
